messages:
mira: Quick update from today's quant bakeoff on new-7b-v2 — AWQ vs GPTQ. Seeing concentrated per-channel outliers in a few FFN layers (3,6,9). Straight INT8 GPTQ gives ~1.8% MRR regression, AWQ is better but still ~0.9% down. initial metric: perplexity +1.2, MRR -1.8. outlier_ratio logged: layer6=0.07

ton y: can you paste the per-layer numbers? curious if it's one bad channel or many small ones

mira: here's the quick dump from the scanner:```
layer 3: max_ratio=15.2, outlier_ch=2
layer 6: max_ratio=18.9, outlier_ch=4
layer 9: max_ratio=13.1, outlier_ch=1
other layers: max_ratio<6, outlier_ch=0
```

shane: that's classic high-kappa channels. proposal: try "channel-surgery" first — detect channels with scale>10 and apply local rescale/clipping then renormalize weights. If a layer has >3 outlier channels, fallback to skip-quantize for that layer (keep fp16).

eva: perf implications? we need numbers for hosted SLA and dedicated throughput profiles

mira: measured locally on a 7b run: baseline fp16 latency (single token) 35ms. AWQ + channel-surgery 28ms. GPTQ int8 (no mitigations) 22ms but unacceptable quality. GPTQ + skip-layer (layers 6 kept fp16) 30ms. Memory delta for skip-layers: +0.6GB on 7b. Quality deltas: AWQ+surg MRR -0.9%, GPTQ+skip MRR -0.2%.

ton y: good tradeoffs. For hosted plans we should prefer AWQ + channel-surgery (lower risk). For Dedicated customers who commit to reserved capacity we can offer GPTQ+skip for cost efficiency. Document both rollout profiles.

shane: implementation notes: adding surgery is cheap at load-time. Pseudocode we tested:```
for channel in layer.channels:
  if scale[channel] > CLIP_TH:
    weights[channel] = weights[channel] * (CLIP_TH/scale[channel])
normalize_layer(weights)
```
We should autotune CLIP_TH per model (start with 10).

mira: also adding an automated bring-up check: `layer_fingerprint.py --threshold 10 --out report.json` which creates recommendations: ["surgery:layers=[3,6,9]","skip:layers=[6]"] and a human-review link.

quant-bot: Bakeoff finished. Summary uploaded to uploads/1778888888/bakeoff-summary.json (includes evals on smol-xsum, smol-retrieval).

eva: runtime fallback policy request: if a live shift causes token-level divergence >5% vs baseline eval, route requests to fp16 variant. That avoids user-facing regressions while we hotfix.

shane: will add `fallback_policy` config to model manifest: ```fallback_policy: {type: "model_variant", condition: "outlier_ratio>0.05", action: "route:fp16"}```. I'll open infra ticket for rollout gating across regions.

ton y: can we add a small eval-run after surgery to verify no heavy hallucination regressions? quick smoke on 2k QA pairs should suffice.

mira: agreed. running smoke now — will attach final numbers. uploaded patch: https://redwood.internal/patches/12345 (surgery + fingerprint tool + docs).

eva: create infra ticket?

mira: created ticket #2346 and linked patch. planning to ship surgery as opt-in on hosted canary, enable by default on dedicated after 2% sample pass.

shane: timeline OK. I'll add metrics (outlier_ratio histogram) to model dashboards and expose `per_layer_outlier` in the console.

mira: thanks — next steps: (1) land surgery patch, (2) add fingerprint to bring-up, (3) add runtime fallback, (4) schedule canary. Will post results here when smoke completes. :rocket:
